A brick badger backing out of a hole in the cut face with a mouthful of brown flexible root tubes trailing behind it.
Trans-clear rain rods slanting into the open trench and beading in bright drops along the top course of tan plates.
A brick sheep leaning over the lip with its front hooves planted, chewing steadily through a taut guy-line.
The spoil cone slumping all at once, the plank across it sliding sideways and the shovel toppling handle-first into the trench.
A swirl of loose tan studs lifting off the spoil heap and carrying across the trench floor in a low skimming arc.
A kettle boiling over on the brick fire, a curling trail of white cloud-slope bricks rising from the spout.
A brick dog down on the swept tile floor digging its own small hole, studs spraying back between its hind legs.
One wicker basket tipping off the lip and landing upside down on the floor, broken pottery pieces scattering across the tiles.
A bucket on the tripod rope swinging wide and clipping a sieve off its stack, the mesh bouncing across the floor.
A flock of brick crows settling in a line along the tent ridge, the nearest one gripping something small and bright in its beak.
Water rising fast in the low corner of the trench, trans-blue plates already lapping over the bottom floor tiles.
A brick goat planted on the tent ridge on all four hooves, the whole canvas sagging and the poles bowing outward beneath it.
A gust pinning the tarpaulin flat against the spoil cone, the weighted corner stones tumbling loose down the slope after it.
A mole-hill of loose studs erupting through the middle of the swept tile floor with a ring of scattered grit around it.
A brick chicken on top of the spoil heap scratching hard, sending a shower of tan studs rattling down one side.
A slab of stacked plates letting go from the cut face and sliding out across the floor in a wide spray of studs.
Frost smoke curling off the wet floor tiles in pale drifts of white cloud-slope bricks catching the first light of the morning.
A barrow rolling away on its own down the turf slope, loose studs spilling steadily out over the rim of the pan.
A brick badger nosing along the base of the cut face, one forepaw hooked under a loose brown root tube pulling it free.
A swarm of trans-clear bubble elements drifting slowly upward out of a shallow puddle of trans-blue plates in the trench floor.
A great rolling mass of white cloud-slope bricks moving in low over the field wall and pressing down toward the open trench.
A brick crow dropping from the tent ridge to the lip and stabbing its beak into the turf mosaic, a tan stud caught in it.
The canvas tarpaulin catching a gust and billowing up off the trench, one corner stone spinning free down the spoil heap.
A brick sheep with both front legs over the lip, its wool-plate sides brushing the cut face as it stretches downward.
Trans-blue plates spreading fast from the low corner, the nearest floor tile already sitting beneath a thin skin of water.
